functions.name: core_nvm_read
functions.signature: core_nvm_read(uint32_t offset, void * buf, uint32_t len)
functions.brief: Read bytes from NVM. offset: byte offset within NVM region (0 to CORE_NVM_SIZE-1) buf:    destination buffer len:    number of bytes to read Returns 0 on success, -1 if out of range.

functions.name: core_nvm_write
functions.signature: core_nvm_write(uint32_t offset, const void * data, uint32_t len)
functions.brief: Write bytes to NVM. offset: byte offset within NVM region (0 to CORE_NVM_SIZE-1) data:   source buffer len:    number of bytes to write Returns 0 on success, -1 if out of range or write error.

functions.name: core_nvm_size
functions.brief: Returns the total NVM size in bytes for this Core.

functions.name: core_nvm_erase
functions.brief: Erase the entire NVM region. Touches every backing sector with a flash erase, no reads — the post-condition is the platform's erased pattern (0xFF for STM32 internal flash). Why this exists separately from `core_nvm_write`: - core_nvm_write does read-modify-write, so if existing NVM contents trigger an ECC fault (e.g., a half-programmed qword from older firmware that used the wrong programming granularity), the write path can't even start. - core_nvm_erase doesn't read, so it always succeeds on a responsive flash controller. Use this: - During development to recover from a corrupt NVM state. - On first boot of a freshly-provisioned device where you don't trust the factory pattern. Returns 0 on success, -1 if any sector erase fails.
